text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures were little changed in late dealings, but continued to lag behind other bond markets as traders grew nervous about the German market's recent fast gains. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 98.81, down 0.04 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures endured a topsy-turvy session, ending virtually flat having traded more than half-a-point higher at one stage. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-18/32, up 03/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures rallied to reach a new contract high for the third consecutive day on Friday before a wave of profit-taking ahead of the weekend sent the contract back close to Thursday's closing level. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.84, up 0.06 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets ended exhausted but happy after a fierce rally prompted by investors piling in on prospects of tougher than expected 1997 budget. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 121.76, up 1.33 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were mixed in moderate midday trade as some profit-taking in the middle of the yield curve poured cold water in the morning rally and took prices off the day's highs, analysts said. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-22/32, down 04/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.89 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures lost half a point during the day, due to a media report which said the Bank of Japan is concerned about any excessive decline in long-term interest rates. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 121.63, down 0.22 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity on Friday was limited as the market took time to absorb the high volumes of deals launched this week. The IMF/World Bank meeting, which starts tomorrow and runs through to October 3, was likely to keep many borrowers out of the market next week, dealers said. A number of dollar issues were expected, though. On Monday the City of Yokohama was likely to launch a $200 million 10-year deal. Spread talk was 25 to 27 basis points over U.S. Treasury bonds.
Suedwestdeutsche Landesbank may also come to the market.
